findings.finding: MapLibre React Native mapStyle is required. The controlled excerpt lacked it and failed current declaration checking. All controlled excerpts now include the matching explicit style URL.

The MapLibre wrapper declares maxBounds as a flat four-number tuple despite its SDK allowing broader bounds-like input. The Mapbox entry inherits SDK bounds-like input. Common bounds require entry-specific conversion.

The flyTo convenience helper sets center/duration without an explicit mode. Android CameraStop defaults EASE; iOS parsing defaults flight. The equivalent flight excerpt now uses setCamera with animationMode flyTo. This source observation does not verify an actual animation.
Convenience CameraRef commands are declared void, while implementation arrows return the Promise from setStop. Neither annotation nor delegation establishes animation-completion timing.

The Mapbox wrapper refreshes style components on styledata; MapLibre does so on style.load. Both SDKs expose style.load. An adapter readiness contract cannot treat wrapper style-data callbacks as equivalent.

Mapbox wrapper proxy distinguishes proposed and controlled transforms. MapLibre wrapper installs its renderer camera-update callback and applies controlled props to proposed updates. Native declarative targets and event callbacks do not prove rejection/clamping equivalence.

The inspected Android wrappers divide projected renderer points by display density and multiply inverse-projection input by it. Adapters must avoid duplicate conversions; multi-density/padding/resize runtime cases remain required.

Native MapLibre documents zoom/double-tap coupling and separately applies explicit Android flags. Both browser handlers provide independent pinch-rotation disabling. Physical gestures and combined defaults still need S06b evidence.
